faqs.a: Organic certification is an official certification process for producers of organic food and other organic agricultural products. In general, any business directly involved in food production can be certified, including seed suppliers, farmers, food processors, retailers, and restaurants. "Certified Organic" assures that products were produced and/or processed under strict conditions required by National Standards (NPOP) and international standards for Organic Production.

faqs.q: How long will it take for my agricultural land to be certified organic?
faqs.a: Conversion duration depends on the cropping history of your operation and your current compliance with certification standards and regulations. Under NPOP standards, it takes two years of managed conversion for annual crops and three years for perennial crops before products can achieve full Organic status.

faqs.q: Is it possible to certify only part of the farm holding (Split / Parallel Production)?
faqs.a: Yes. GOPCA supports part certification of a farm holding, provided there is a clear, time-bound conversion plan for the remaining area. Stringent physical buffer zones and distinct recordkeeping must prevent any co-mingling. Simultaneous production of identical conventional and organic varieties that cannot be visually distinguished is strictly prohibited.

faqs.q: What are the main stages in the GOPCA certification process?
faqs.a: The certification cycle comprises: 1) Application submission with Farm Map, Field History, and Organic System Plan (OSP); 2) Document verification and fee assessment; 3) On-site announced or unannounced physical inspection by accredited GOPCA inspectors; 4) Mandatory soil, leaf, and produce residue sampling; 5) Non-compliance closure by operator; 6) Review by the GOPCA Evaluation Committee; and 7) Scope Certificate issuance via APEDA TraceNet.

faqs.q: What inputs are permitted during conversion and organic maintenance?
faqs.a: Only bio-fertilizers, organic manures, bio-pesticides, and commercial inputs certified and listed on the GOPCA Approved Inputs List or complying with NPOP Appendix 1 and 2 are permissible. All chemical fertilizers (Urea, DAP, etc.), synthetic pesticides, herbicides, GMO seeds, and sewage sludge are categorically prohibited.

faqs.q: How does GOPCA certify Organic Grower Groups under the Internal Control System (ICS)?
faqs.a: Grower Groups comprise smallholder farmers in geographical proximity operating an Internal Control System (ICS). The group must maintain 100% internal inspections of all member plots annually. GOPCA conducts external surveillance audits, inspecting the mandated square-root percentage of members, testing soil and crop samples, and auditing warehouse and handling records.

faqs.q: How do operators submit certification fees to GOPCA?
faqs.a: Operators can deposit inspection and certification fees directly using the official GOPCA Bharat QR / UPI Code or through RTGS/NEFT to GOPCA bank accounts. The transaction reference number and counterfoil must be uploaded with the application dossier for receipt generation.
